rationale:
Assessed major compatibility impact from v1.1.0; selected a minor bump to 1.2.0 under the maintainer-approved persistent pre-production policy.

The maintainer explicitly authorized replacing the premature 2.0.0 release identity, publishing consistent 1.2.0 metadata and images, and removing the old release/tag/image aliases after replacement verification. The exact withdrawn commit is 806039e9403a99a24e234b0f0cd2ef7326226e77. The replacement preserves application behavior and migrations from that commit. It adds the release phase policy, guarded replacement preparation, regression coverage, explicit GitHub Latest selection and a manually dispatched, narrowly scoped image-cleanup workflow. Production deployment remains a separate authorization.

- HTTP (breaking relative to 1.1.0): POST /v1/memory-processing/consent is replaced by /provider, capabilities replace consents/consentVersion with options, and shared consent contracts are removed. Evidence: packages/shared/src/memory-processing.ts, apps/api/src/memory-processing/memory-processing.controller.ts and docs/openapi.json.
- Authority (breaking relative to 1.1.0): independent owner-selected providers authorize extraction and consolidation without a separate TypeSafe consent toggle. Explicit revocations map to OpenAI, other owners inherit instance defaults, and configured TypeSafe is preferred when task defaults are unset. The selector has no off state. Evidence: docs/adr/0046-owner-selected-memory-processing-providers.md, apps/api/src/memory-processing and packages/db/prisma/migrations/20260924010000_processing_provider_preference.
- MCP and identity/OAuth: tool contracts, transports, grants, accounts and sessions remain compatible with 1.1.0. Reconnect active voice sessions to use the extraction-only configuration fingerprint. Evidence: unchanged packages/mcp/src/tools.ts and auth/OAuth contracts plus the published provider-selection assessment.
- Data: the additive preference migration preserves existing vault data and audit history. Export v2 remains supported and adds optional preferences; JSON import is not a backup and does not restore processing history/provider choices. Back up the database, stop old processing services, migrate and start matching images when upgrading from 1.1.0. Rollback to 1.1.0 requires its pre-upgrade database. Evidence: migration SQL, packages/shared/src/data-control.ts, apps/api/src/data-control and CHANGELOG.md.
- Deployment: image/service names, Node/pnpm requirements and environment variable names remain compatible. Review MEMORY_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM and MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_SYSTEM because their defaults now initialize owner choices. The numbering correction changes image versions only; it does not modify application source, dependency versions, Dockerfile or database migrations relative to the withdrawn build. The live website currently identifies the withdrawn build, so old image cleanup waits for deployment reconciliation.
- Compatible fixes preserved: consolidation-toggle persistence, completed exclusion reporting, actionable failure/deferred reasons and transcript-bound voice extraction feedback. Evidence: existing provider-selection release notes and tests, unchanged by this correction.

Version arithmetic and verification retain phase and impact separately. Future breaking pre-production releases advance within 1.x, compatible fixes use patches, and an explicit production-phase change restores normal semantic versioning. Existing CI, fingerprint, merge ancestry and publication gates remain required.
